# 04-memory-and-retrieval - Memory and retrieval

## Why this topic exists

A context window is finite and a model's weights are fixed at training time. This topic covers bringing outside facts in at request time, and then the follow-on problem of deciding what stays in the window once there is more material than room.

## Prerequisite topics

None. This topic is an entry point.

## Papers in this topic

### Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus and others (2020)

- arXiv: [2005.11401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)
- PDF: [`2005.11401-rag.pdf`](pdf/2005.11401-rag.pdf)
- Notes: [`2005.11401-rag.md`](notes/2005.11401-rag.md)
- Tier: core, read first

Read this for the original framing of retrieval as a component of generation rather than a preprocessing step.

### MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Kevin Lin and others (2023)

- arXiv: [2310.08560](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560)
- PDF: [`2310.08560-memgpt.pdf`](pdf/2310.08560-memgpt.pdf)
- Notes: [`2310.08560-memgpt.md`](notes/2310.08560-memgpt.md)
- Tier: deep, read after the core paper in its topic

Read this for the analogy between managing a context window and managing virtual memory.
